learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the fuel that powers the world! Learn the chemistry of Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes, and unlock the unique aromatic stability of Benzene rings.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Carbon chains with only single bonds (formula $C_nH_{2n+2}$). Also known as 'Paraffins' because they are highly unreactive. Their main reaction is free radical substitution (like halogenation in presence of UV light).
Contain at least one C=C double bond ($C_nH_{2n}$). The pi bond makes them highly reactive, causing them to undergo 'Electrophilic Addition' reactions, breaking the double bond to add new atoms.

When adding an unsymmetrical reagent (like $HBr$) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part of the reagent ($Br^-$) goes to the carbon atom with FEWER hydrogen atoms! (The rich get richer with Hydrogens).
Contain C≡C triple bonds ($C_nH_{2n-2}$). The unique thing about terminal alkynes is that the hydrogen attached to the triple-bonded carbon is actually quite acidic and can be replaced by metals!

Cyclic, highly stable compounds. Even though Benzene ($C_6H_6$) has three double bonds, it doesn't undergo addition reactions easily because of 'Resonance' (the electrons run in a continuous circle). It prefers Electrophilic Substitution.

fun_activity.title: 🍌 The Fruit Ripening Gas
fun_activity.instructions: Place a green, unripe banana in a sealed brown paper bag with a fully ripe apple. Check it in two days—the banana will be yellow! The ripe apple naturally releases Ethene (Ethylene) gas, a simple alkene that acts as a powerful plant hormone to trigger ripening.

exam_tips: 📌 Ozonolysis of alkenes is a favorite exam question. It cleaves the double bond completely, producing aldehydes or ketones, and is used to locate the exact position of the double bond in an unknown alkene.
📌 Anti-Markovnikov's rule (Peroxide Effect / Kharasch effect) applies ONLY to the addition of $HBr$ in the presence of organic peroxides. It does not work for $HCl$ or $HI$.
📌 To check if a compound is Aromatic, use Huckel's Rule: It must be cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and have exactly $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons (where $n = 0, 1, 2...$).
quick_recap: ⭐ Wurtz reaction takes two alkyl halides and sodium metal to produce a symmetrical alkane with DOUBLE the number of carbon atoms (It cannot produce Methane!).
⭐ Benzene undergoes Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$.
⭐ Boiling points of alkanes increase with molecular mass but decrease with chain branching (branched chains have less surface area for Van der Waals forces).
